> `Get-FileHash <file>`). These notes aren't signed, so that doesn't prove who built it. The source: https://github.com/BlueHeisenberg/SCSKiller/tree/v1.4.8.
>
> Smart App Control (Windows 11) blocks unsigned apps outright, with no Run anyway.

**New on Windows**

- Hunt: Showdown 1896 compiles from its game files on NVIDIA. On AMD, on the game's current build, it compiles part of
  its shaders from the game's files, about half of what the game built in a measured session, and the rest still
  compiles while you play. The game contains anti-cheat. Enabling the recorder in it is at your own risk, and SCSKiller
  isn't responsible for bans.

**Changed**

- RE Requiem's recorder is off by default instead of blocked, and the recorder switch on its page turns it on.
- No game key is in SCSKiller's code, binaries or server. Encrypted RE Engine and FromSoftware games download their
  key at run time from its public source, and Unreal Engine games that need one read it from the game's exe or from
  the key you enter on the game's page, the others show as encrypted.

**Improved**

- The compile size limit on a game's page is No limit or Custom size, set with a number box or a slider from 1 to 128
  GB, or with presets of 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 GB.
- Encrypted RE Engine and FromSoftware games whose key can't be downloaded say so in their status and show a key field
  to add it by hand.
- Encrypted RE Engine and FromSoftware DirectX 12 games without a key are recorded while you play and compile what was
  recorded, and the key adds the rest.
- Frostbite games such as Dead Space have their shaders read from the game's files. DirectX 12 ones still need a
  recording.
- When the recorder didn't load in a game's last launch, its status asks you to send a report instead of asking for
  another recording.
- Games the recorder can't run in say they can't be compiled yet, instead of asking for a recording.
- On a first run, the recorders wait until the Welcome is answered.

**Improved on Windows**

- With AMD and NVIDIA, encrypted RE Engine and FromSoftware DirectX 11 games without a key, and DirectX 11 games whose
  shaders are packed, are recorded while you play and compile what was recorded.
- A start no longer reads every game's exe again for the AMD checks when the game hasn't changed.

**Fixed**

- Opening the window no longer takes gigabytes of memory for a few seconds while the Library loads its game icons.
- Reading a game's shaders in the background no longer takes most of the PC's memory.
- A game's shaders read for the recorder in the background no longer start over again and again while other games
  compile.
- A stopped background read of an older Unreal game's shaders goes on where it stopped instead of starting over.
- The first scan is faster on large Unreal Engine games.
- Rescans are faster after you play a large Unreal Engine game.
- The Epic library no longer lists Unreal Engine and plugin installs as games, which made the first scan slow.
- Epic games, Fortnite included, stay in the library while the Epic Games Launcher updates them, and a Fortnite added by
  hand gets the Normal and Performance modes.
- Games whose exe holds a very large icon show their icon in the library again.
- Half-Life 2 and other games that ship DXVK for an optional Vulkan renderer read as DirectX 9.
- A game whose exe imports DirectX 10 but makes a DirectX 11 device, such as Ryse: Son of Rome, is read as DirectX 11.
- Games that run on DirectX 11 or 12 no longer show 0% covered after a DirectX 11 compile.
- Hookshot ports installed with their launcher beside a bin folder are detected as Vulkan games.

detail.readme:
SCSKiller

Shader Compilation Stutter Killer. SCSKiller compiles your games' shaders into your GPU driver's cache before you play, so the game doesn't stop to compile them mid-game. Free and open source, for Windows.

Website · Download · Patreon · Discord · X · Report a bug · Request a game

> [!WARNING] > The only official downloads are this repository's [Releases](https://github.com/BlueHeisenberg/SCSKiller/releases). > See [official links](#official-links) for the accounts and sites that belong to SCSKiller.

## Why A game that meets a new effect has the GPU driver compile its shader on the spot, and the frame waits: that's shader compilation stutter. SCSKiller reads the shaders a game ships with, works out the pipelines it will build, and compiles them into the driver's cache ahead of time, in its own process with the game closed. ## Results About 5 minutes of play per game, from a cold driver cache and after compiling with SCSKiller. A stutter is a shader compile the game waited 20 ms or more for.

Measured with SCSKiller's recorder. Your numbers depend on the game, GPU and driver. SCSKiller fixes shader compilation stutter only, not traversal or streaming stutter, and a shader it couldn't find or record can still compile in game. ## Features - **NVIDIA and AMD**, DirectX 12 games, and DirectX 11 games on NVIDIA. - **Finds your games** in Steam, Epic Games, EA app, GOG, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox (PC), Battle.net, PURPLE, HoYoPlay, Gaijin and the Riot Client, plus games you add yourself. - **Puts games known to stutter on top**, with the reason, and marks games whose engine prepares its shaders itself. - **Compiles again after a driver update**, which clears the shader cache, on its own if you let it. - **Optional recorder** for games whose pipelines its files don't give: play a few minutes with it on, then compile. It also records alongside a mod that replaces shaders. - **Frame times per session**: with the recorder on, a game's page graphs your last session and marks shader stutters apart from other hitches. They stay on your PC. - **Play button** that starts the game through its store. - **Community shader hash database** for Patreon supporters: other players' recordings, so your games are covered without recording them first. Sharing yours is opt-in, anonymous and hash-only. - **Leaves anti-cheat games alone** beyond reading their files: no launching, no injecting, no recorder, except in a session you allow per game and confirm every launch, at your own risk: without EasyAntiCheat for ELDEN RING and ARMORED CORE VI, or in games with anti-cheat once you turn on "Allow the recorder in games with anti-cheat (at your own risk)". ## Install | Requirement | | |---|---| | OS | Windows 10 (version 2004) or 11, 64-bit | | GPU | NVIDIA or AMD | | Games | DirectX 12, DirectX 11 on NVIDIA | Intel GPUs aren't supported yet: I don't have one to test on. If you'd like to sponsor an Intel Arc GPU, get in touch at [contact@scskiller.com](mailto:contact@scskiller.com). Download `SCSKiller-Setup.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/BlueHeisenberg/SCSKiller/releases/latest) and run it. It installs for your user only, needs no admin rights and updates itself. Or unzip `SCSKiller--Portable.zip` to any folder you can write to and run `SCSKiller.exe`. It updates itself too, and keeps its settings and data in a `data` folder beside the exe. Turn recording off for your games before you delete the folder, so the recorder leaves the game folders. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Releases aren't code-signed yet**, so the first run will probably show SmartScreen's "Windows protected your PC". > Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. Updates never show it. To check a download, compare its SHA-256 with the > one in the release notes (PowerShell: `Get-FileHash `). Smart App Control (Windows 11) blocks unsigned apps > outright, with no Run anyway. ## How to use it 1. **Open SCSKiller.** It finds your games and the shaders they ship with. 2. **Queue games and press Compile.** "Add all recommended" is a good start. Keep the game closed while it compiles. 3. **Play**, from your store or with the Play button. SCSKiller can be closed. Left open, it checks that the compile reached the cache the game really uses, and with the recorder on, the game's page shows your session's frame times and anything that still compiled. If a game needs a recording, turn on **Record**, play it for a few minutes, then compile it.

## FAQ **Can I get banned?** SCSKiller only reads the files of games with anti-cheat and adds its recorder to them only in a session you allow and confirm (next question). Its anti-cheat check can still miss a game, so you use SCSKiller at your own risk, and its authors are not responsible for bans, crashes or lost data. **Is it safe with anti-cheat games?** Outside a session SCSKiller never launches them, injects into them or gives them the recorder. It only reads their files. A session is allowed per game, confirmed every launch, and at your own risk. The offline session for ELDEN RING and ARMORED CORE VI runs them offline without EasyAntiCheat when their exe is started directly: Steam must be running (offline mode is fine), and SCSKiller adds `d3d12.dll`, `scskiller.cfg` and `steam_appid.txt` to the game's folder and starts the exe itself. With "Allow the recorder in games with anti-cheat (at your own risk)" on in Settings, any other supported game can run a session too: SCSKiller starts the game as usual, with `d3d12.dll` and `scskiller.cfg` in its folder. Enabling the recorder in games with anti-cheat is at your own risk. SCSKiller isn't responsible for bans. Bans from it are not support issues. In both kinds the recorder records only that process. When the game exits, SCSKiller takes those files out again (each only while it is still the file it added) and keeps the recording and the session's frame times, at the next logon or start if SCSKiller was closed or the PC crashed. If those files are still there when you start the game online, you could be banned. Don't uninstall SCSKiller while the game runs. **What does it write, and where?** Settings and per-game plans go in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\SCSKiller\` (the `data` folder of a portable copy), and the compiled pipelines go in your driver's own shader cache. Game files are never modified. The optional recorder adds `d3d12.dll` and `scskiller.cfg` to the folder of a game you turn it on for, and turning it off removes exactly those files. On a new install it goes in no game folder until you close the welcome, whose box sets "Record in all compatible games". It never goes into a game with anti-cheat, and comes out the moment SCSKiller finds anti-cheat: when it scans, when the game exits or updates, and every 2 minutes while it runs. `scskiller.cfg` names the game's exe as it was when SCSKiller last found no anti-cheat in its folders, and a game records only while its exe is still that one and no anti-cheat is next to it. Uninstalling SCSKiller removes these files and the recordings from every game folder, and a scan removes them from a game Steam uninstalled. **Does it touch my drivers or their settings?** No. It compiles through DirectX, as the game would. **Do I need an account?** No. Everything the app does on your PC is free. Signing in with Patreon adds the supporter features. **My game isn't detected, or something broke.** Open an [issue](https://github.com/BlueHeisenberg/SCSKiller/issues/new/choose) with the bug or game request template. ## Support the project The app is free and stays free. [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/SCSKiller) pays for the servers behind the community database. Sign in with Patreon in Settings to unlock your tier. | Tier | You get | |---|---| | **Patreon supporter** | The community shader hash database, and beta builds | | **Patreon backer** | All of that, plus alpha builds and priority on game requests | ## Build from source Visual Studio 2022 (C++ desktop workload with CMake) and the .NET 10 SDK: ``` cmake -S proxy -B proxy/build -A x64 cmake --build proxy/build --config Release dotnet build SCSKiller.slnx -c Release ``` `build/publish.ps1` builds the distribution into `dist\`. Design: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). Contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Changes: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Security issues go through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), never a public issue. ## Official links - GitHub: https://github.com/BlueHeisenberg/SCSKiller - Website: https://scskiller.com - Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/SCSKiller - Discord: https://discord.gg/st7C4yCTcN - X: https://x.com/SCSKiller Anything else claiming to be SCSKiller isn't. Please [report it](https://github.com/BlueHeisenberg/SCSKiller/issues/new/choose). ## Licence GPL-3.0-or-later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)), with an additional permission for Oodle, the Windows App SDK and graphics driver libraries ([LICENSE-EXCEPTION.txt](LICENSE-EXCEPTION.txt)). Not affiliated with any GPU maker, engine maker or game publisher. All product names are trademarks of their owners. ### Forks Forks are welcome under the licence. Please give yours its own name, say it's unofficial and based on SCSKiller, and keep the SCSKiller copyright notices. The measurements and screenshots in this README are SCSKiller's own, so please don't present them as a fork's. Official builds come only from this repository's [Releases](https://github.com/BlueHeisenberg/SCSKiller/releases) page. A fork's builds, bugs and anti-cheat behaviour are its author's: SCSKiller keeps its recorder out of anti-cheat games except in a session the user confirms, and can't vouch for a fork that changes that. Improvements are always welcome back here as pull requests. Fixes, games and ideas from forks make SCSKiller better for everyone.
